svg.aria-label: How to write ぜ: 5 strokes · 4 pen lifts · 7 movements
svg.title: Writing ぜ
svg.desc: 7 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ぜ (japanese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansJP-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/0305c.svg, hiragana ぜ (U+305C HIRAGANA LETTER ZE), five stroke paths kvg:0305c-s1 to s5 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0) <https://github.com/KanjiVG/kanjivg/blob/master/kanji/0305c.svg>. Source note on variation: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 to s3 are せ's strokes, the same paths as in its file for せ, kanji/0305b.svg; s4 and s5 are the dakuten, the left tick first and then the right one, each drawn down to the right. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. KanjiVG draws the right stem second and the left stem third, as its file for せ, kanji/0305b.svg, does. This inventory's せ row, which cites Sirgazil's animation, has those two the other way round; this path follows KanjiVG.
svg.text: How it is written — 5 strokes · 4 pen lifts · 7 movements
Stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/0305c.svg, hiragana ぜ (U+305C HIRAGANA LETTER ZE), five stroke paths kvg:0305c-s1 to s5 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
